title: Hospital operations Eisenhower matrix
goal: An operations manager can separate urgent work from important work at a glance.

rubric.must: All four Eisenhower action quadrants are visibly labelled.
Each named work item is positioned in a clear urgency-importance quadrant.
Urgency and importance axes are visibly directional.
At least one item is visible in each action type.
Labels remain readable in the plot.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the matrix/quadrant exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The target shows all five work items in clear quadrants, directional urgency and importance axes, and readable labels. Each action type has at least one item; no material overlap or cropping is visible.

items.evidence: All four quadrants are labelled: Schedule, Do now, Eliminate, and Delegate.

Restore medication scanner and Approve staffing roster are in the high-importance, high-urgency quadrant; Review infection dashboard is high-importance, low-urgency; Reply to vendor survey is low-importance, high-urgency; Reformat old slides is low-importance, low-urgency.
Urgency increases to the right, indicated by the right-pointing horizontal axis arrow; importance increases upward, indicated by the upward vertical axis arrow.
The Schedule, Do now, Delegate, and Eliminate quadrants each contain at least one work item.
All five work-item labels are readable within the plot, with no visible material overlap or cropping.
